questions.stem: What happens to surface area to volume ratio as an organism grows larger?

options.text: It decreases, leaving less exchange surface per unit of volume
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: It increases, easing exchange
options.explanation: Volume grows faster than surface area, so the ratio falls.

options.text: It stays constant at all sizes
options.explanation: The two scale differently, so the ratio changes.

options.text: It doubles with every size doubling
options.explanation: No such fixed doubling exists.

questions.stem: Why do larger organisms evolve specialised exchange surfaces?

options.text: To eliminate the need for blood supply
options.explanation: Good blood supply accompanies these surfaces.

options.text: To raise the surface area available for diffusion despite their low surface area to volume ratio
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: To shorten their digestion time
options.explanation: Exchange surfaces serve diffusion, not digestion speed.

options.text: To reduce their overall volume
options.explanation: The volume stays; the surface is what is increased.

questions.stem: Which adaptation is cited for cells specialised for diffusion?

options.text: Fewer organelles to make room
options.explanation: Space inside the cell is not the limiting factor.

options.text: Lower temperature inside the cell
options.explanation: Cooler particles move more slowly.

options.text: Increased surface area, as in root hair cells and ileum lining cells
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: Thicker walls to slow escape
options.explanation: Thicker walls would slow crossing, not speed it.

questions.stem: How does temperature raise the rate of movement across a membrane?

options.text: Warmth widens the membrane's pores
options.explanation: The membrane does not open pores when heated.

options.text: Warmth dissolves the membrane
options.explanation: The membrane stays intact across the normal range.

options.text: Warmth increases the concentration gradient
options.explanation: Gradient is a separate factor.

options.text: Warmer particles carry more kinetic energy and strike the membrane more often
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

questions.stem: Why does a steeper concentration gradient speed up exchange?

options.text: More particles sit on the crowded side, so more random collisions send them across
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: Particles gain energy from the gradient
options.explanation: The gradient adds no energy; it adds pressure of numbers.

options.text: The membrane opens wider for steep gradients
options.explanation: Membrane permeability is independent of gradient.

options.text: Steep gradients shorten the diffusion distance
options.explanation: Distance is governed by wall thickness, not gradient.

questions.stem: Name the four factors that influence the rate of movement of substances.
questions.modelAnswer: The surface-to-volume balance, the travel distance, the temperature, and the gradient's steepness.

questions.stem: State why alveoli and capillary walls are one cell thick.
questions.modelAnswer: To keep the diffusion distance minimal so gases cross rapidly between air and blood.

questions.stem: Explain why a highly folded surface, such as the intestine lining, speeds absorption.
questions.modelAnswer: Folding packs far more membrane into the same space, which raises the surface area available for diffusion; with more area, more particles can cross at the same moment, so absorption proceeds faster per unit of volume.

questions.stem: A single-celled pond organism and a large mammal exchange substances with their surroundings. Explain why only one needs specialised exchange organs.
questions.modelAnswer: The pond cell is small, so its surface area to volume ratio stays high and plain diffusion supplies it; the mammal is large, its ratio is low, so it needs surfaces such as alveoli with rich blood supply to restore exchange speed.
